name: Roger Wicker

issue_poll.name: Cygnal Mississippi likely-voter survey, Aug 26–27, 2024; Gallup national issue-importance poll, Sept 16–28, 2024
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–4 from the Cygnal MS poll (economy, tax policy, health care, crime, in reported order; only partial shares published). Ranks 5–10 fill from Gallup national 'extremely important' shares (https://news.gallup.com/file/poll/651749/2024_10_09_Vote%20Issues%20Topline%20and%20Tabs.pdf). State-only items (ballot initiative) skipped.

issues.position: Said prices and taxes were lower under Trump; no specific plan

issues.note: H.R.1 made the 2017 individual tax cuts permanent.

issues.position: Block HHS nursing home staffing rule; make telehealth permanent

votes.bill_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (staffing rule delayed 10 years)
votes.question: On passage

issues.note: Telehealth got only short-term extensions in spending bills, not a permanent-law vote.

issues.position: No specific forward position found; fentanyl sanctions law already enacted
issues.note: FEND Off Fentanyl Act (his bill) became law in April 2024: past record, not a promise.
Not a cosponsor of the 2024 SAVE Act (S.4292).

issues.position: Raise defense spending toward 5% of GDP

votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for FY2026
votes.question: On passage

issues.note: H.R.1 added about $150B for defense; NDAA passed 77-20 (https://www.dailypress.senate.gov/thursday-october-9-2025/).

issues.position: Build border wall; pass the Laken Riley Act

votes.bill_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (border wall funding)
votes.question: On passage

issues.position: Backed School Choice Week resolution; no specific policy
issues.note: Joined Educational Choice for Children Act in Feb 2025, after the campaign.
No Senate floor vote on gun restrictions found this term.

caveats: No Mississippi poll with a full ranked issue list was found; the top 10 combines a partial Cygnal state poll with national Gallup data.
Tax position comes from an official Senate statement dated Nov 12, 2024, one week after Election Day; his campaign closing message only cited lower taxes under Trump.

Roll call numbers not confirmed for Laken Riley Act passage (S.5, Jan 20, 2025) or NDAA passage (S.2296, Oct 9, 2025); his Yea votes inferred from his office's release and from his role as NDAA sponsor.
H.R.1 is counted for four issues (taxes, health care, national security, immigration), each for a separate provision.
